title: Memory graft quarantine + KV journal reconcile for cross-env fragmentation leading to GPU OOMs
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Summary:
Several customers across Hosted, Dedicated and Private tiers reported spikes in latency followed by GPU OOMs during large-chat bursts. Root cause analysis indicates a correlated sequence: an allocator 'graft' event (cross-shard memory refactor) exposed a small window where KV journal writes could drift from the in-memory KV index. Over time the drift produces ghost entries and tombstone miscounts that increase fragmentation and reduce available contiguous GPU page allocations. When large-session prefix/KV caches were loaded concurrently, the allocator could not satisfy large contiguous allocations and triggered OOMs.

What we observed:
- Incidents concentrated on multi-tenant hosts and some Dedicated nodes with long-lived sessions and prefix caching enabled.
- Symptoms: small, contiguous allocation failures, rapid slab fragmentation, rising tombstone counts on the KV journal, slow KV lookups, increased page allocation retries.
- Customer impact: intermittent 5–30m windows of high error rates (500s + rejected requests) and GPU OOM crashes; affected several enterprise customers (support escalations open).

Immediate mitigations applied (done 2026-03-02 to 2026-03-04):
1) Emergency runtime config change: reduce max contiguous allocation request size on Hosted to force more conservative batching (rolled by Marco, ~20% traffic).
2) Canary emergency rollback: disabled aggressive prefix warmup on 3 Dedicated pools to stop re-triggering large contiguous allocations.
3) Added an ephemeral watchdog to surface tombstone count > threshold to Ops and auto-quarantine sessions creating >10K journal writes/min.

Workplan / technical solution (this ticket):
A) Implement a "memory graft quarantine" mode: when journal/index delta is detected at reconciliation time, automatically place affected session arenas into a soft-quarantine ring. Quarantined arenas are prevented from making large contiguous allocations; they are drained and compacted asynchronously. This is a short-term runtime feature to prevent immediate OOM cascades.
B) KV journal reconciliation: add a lightweight, background reconciler that replays recent KV journal entries with idempotent checksums and rehydrates the in-memory index. The reconciler uses monotonic watermarks so it never reorders committed entries.
C) Index integrity checks: introduce periodic checksum snapshots (per-shard) and a fast verify that runs during compaction. On mismatch, trigger a local reconcile and metric alert.
D) Allocator improvement: a small allocator policy change to prefer hybrid-slab allocations for large prefix caches to avoid starving contiguous page pools. Also add preflight checks to fail gracefully before OOM.

Design decisions and tradeoffs:
- We chose soft-quarantine rather than immediate eviction to avoid data loss and preserve prompt KV coherence for live sessions. This increases background compaction load but minimizes customer-visible failures.
- The reconciler is intentionally conservative (idempotent replays + checksums) to avoid introducing ordering regressions. It will run with a low-priority IO budget to limit impact on latency-critical paths.
- We do not introduce global stop-the-world compaction; all fixes are per-shard and opportunistic to preserve SLA requirements.

Implementation notes / PRs:
- Runtime patch: allocator/graft-quarantine + reconciler implementation (WIP) — PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12874 (draft)
- Unit tests for checksum/verify: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12889 (branch)
- Canary rollout manifest + feature flag: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-config/commit/2a7b3f1

Observability and runbooks:
- New Grafana dashboard panels added to surface: tombstone_count, journal_delta_age, per-shard-checksum_mismatch_rate, large_alloc_failures. Link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/oom-hub/runtime-memory-health
- Runbook steps added to triage playbook: quarantine -> reconcile -> drain -> compact -> resume. See Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Memory+Graft+Quarantine+Runbook

Canary & rollout plan:
1) Merge reconciler/allocator changes behind feature flags (runtime-1.28 branch).
2) Canary on 5% Hosted traffic with additional metrics sampling (72h).
3) If stable, expand to Dedicated warm pools (staged over 3 days).
4) For Private deployments, produce an ops guide and a patch bundle for customers (coordinate with SE team).

Testing and QA:
- Stress test harness updated to simulate long-lived sessions with high journal write rates. Testcases cover: concurrent prefix loads, multi-tenant eviction, and simulated index drift. Test results stored: s3://redwood-artifacts/oom-tests/246910/ (internal).
- Perf regression gate set at <2% p99 latency change; memory flat or improved in synthetic workloads.

Customer comms and tickets referenced:
- Escalation cases: CS-55892 (Hosted enterprise), CS-56110 (Dedicated pharma), CS-56177 (Private on-prem fintech).
- Customer-facing status updates prepared by Solutions (draft in Drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1Graft-Quarantine-Communications

Open questions / risks:
- Background reconciler IO budget: too low and it won't repair quickly; too high and it could impact p99 latency. Need ops/infra input.
- Some legacy Private customers run older runtime builds; coordinating patch deployment takes time and may leave them susceptible longer.

Acceptance criteria (for Done):
- No further P0 OOM escalations from same root cause for 7 days on canary and 72h extended on production pool after rollout.
- Metrics: per-shard checksum_mismatch_rate -> 0 (or within historical baseline) and tombstone_count decreased by >=70% on affected nodes within 24h of reconcile.
- Postmortem document complete linking telemetry, RCA, and long-term mitigation (including allocator redesign roadmap).

Postmortem / follow-ups planned:
- Schedule deep allocator audit with research/infra (Epic: allocator-redesign-2026).
- Evaluate adding transactional KV journal commit markers to reduce future drift.
- Backport reconciler to runtime-1.26 branch used by 3 Private customers.

Owner notes:

- Priya to own customer comms and PM updates.
- Dana Chen (SRE) to sign off on IO budget before canary.
